questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

Neetu have been / waiting for me / since 10 o’clock / in the morning.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Neetu have been.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• In the given sentence, the error lies in the first part.
 
• **The subject "Neetu" is singular, but the verb "have been" is plural. **
 
• **This creates a subject-verb agreement error.**
 
• The correct verb form for "Neetu" would be "has been."
 
• The sentence should read: "Neetu has been waiting for me since 10 o'clock in the morning."

Hence, **the correct answer is option 1**.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

Her dog can climb __under__ the fence.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Over.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Let us understand the meaning of the given and the marked words:
 
 
• **"Under" means below the surface of something; covered by something**.

 
 
• Example: Most of an iceberg is under the water.
 
 
 
• **"Over" means above or higher than something.**
 
 
• Example: He threw a ball over the fence.
 
 
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the dog is climbing under__ the fence, so the opposite would be climbing __over__ the fence.

Hence, **the correct answer is option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• In option 2, Sink: This word means to go down or submerge, which is not the opposite of climbing under something.
 
• In option 3, Behind: This word means at the back of something, which is not the opposite of going under something.
 
• In option 4, Beneath: This word is a synonym of 'under', so it cannot be the antonym.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The company's board of directors will announce the financial results at the annual meeting tomorrow.

options.text: The financial results will have been announced by the company's board of directors at the annual meeting tomorrow.
The financial results are being announced by the company's board of directors at the annual meeting tomorrow.
The company's board of directors announced the financial results at the annual meeting tomorrow.
The financial results will be announced by the company's board of directors at the annual meeting tomorrow.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**The financial results will be announced by the company's board of directors at the annual meeting tomorrow.**" [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• Active voice denotes that the subject is performing the action while passive voice denotes that the subject is acted upon by the verb or action in the sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in active voice, with the subject ("The company's board of directors") performing the action ("will announce the financial results").
 
• **To convert it into passive voice, we need to make the object ("the financial results") the subject of the sentence and add a form of the verb "to be" + past participle of the main verb ("announced").**
 
• **The preposition "at the annual meeting tomorrow" remains at the end of the sentence.**
 
• The final sentence in passive voice will be: "The financial results will be announced by the company's board of directors at the annual meeting tomorrow."

Hence, **the correct answer is option 4**.

__
 
• **The subject "participants" is plural, so the verb should also be plural.**

 
 
• **Thus, we will eliminate the options 2, 3 and 4.**
 
 
 
• Also, "curiously" is an adverb describing how the participants are waiting.
 
• Thus, it can be concluded that the sentence in option 1 is grammatically correct.
 
• The sentence in option 1 has correct subject-verb agreement and proper use of adverb.

Hence, **the correct answer is option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:

options.text: Be forced to explain your actions and (probably) punished

• It is a metaphorical expression, comparing the confusion to knots.
 
• **The sentence suggests that Pooja was unable to articulate the problem clearly.**
 
• The idiom is often used in situations where a person is struggling to express themselves or make sense of something.
 
 
• Example: The minister tied himself in knots answering a touchy political question. 
 
 
 
• Among the given options, the statement in option 2 explains the given idiom appropriately.

Hence, **the correct answer is option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. In Bihar and Central India, in particular, every district had smelters that used local deposits of ore to produce iron which was widely used for the manufacture of implements and tools of daily use.

B. The smelting was done by men while women worked on the bellows, pumping air that kept the charcoal burning.

C. But iron smelting in India was extremely common till the end of the nineteenth century.

D. Production of Wootz steel required a highly specialised technique of refining iron.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**DCAB.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Among the given sentences, Sentence D mentions the subject of the passage.**
 
• **Thus, we will place sentence D at the beginning of the passage.**
 
• Sentence D talks about the production of Wootz steel which required a highly specialized technique of refining iron. This implies that iron smelting was not a simple process.
 
• Further, sentence C states that iron smelting was extremely common in India till the end of the nineteenth century. This indicates that iron smelting was prevalent in India for a long time.
 
• Sentence A mentions that every district in Bihar and Central India had smelters that used local deposits of ore to produce iron. This implies that iron smelting was a widespread activity in India.
 
• Sentence B talks about the division of labor in iron smelting. Men did the smelting while women worked on the bellows. This gives us an idea of how iron smelting was carried out in India.
 
• **Thus, the sentences chronologically explain the prevalence, spread and process of iron smelting in India.**
 
• **Thus, it can be concluded that the correct order for the given sentence would be "DCAB."**

Hence, **the correct answer is option 2**.

__
 
• Homonym is a word that is spelt and pronounced like another word but that has a different meaning.
 
 
• Example: ‘Bank’ [river bank] and ‘bank’ [place where money is kept] are homonyms.
 
 
 
• Now, let us understand the meaning of the given options:
 
 
• "Sense" means common sense or good judgment.
 
• **"Scent" means an odor or trail, whereas "sense" means a feeling or perception.**
 
• "Cense" means to burn incense, which is not relevant to the context of the sentence.
 
• "Cents" refers to a unit of currency, which does not make sense in the context of the sentence.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the word "scent" will fit the best.
 
• The correct sentence will be: The hunter dogs followed the hyena’s **scent**.

Hence, **the correct answer is option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__**
